points.description: States precisely that a static array is initialized only once (the first time the function is called / program-lifetime single initialization), not again on later calls.
points.partial_credit: Half credit (1.5) if it says the static array keeps or retains its values between calls but does not state it is initialized only once.

points.description: Correct contrast: a non-static (automatic/local) array is re-created and re-initialized every time the function is called.
points.partial_credit: Half credit (1) if it only says the non-static array is not preserved between calls, without stating re-initialization on each call.

rubric.notes: Full marks need the precise fact that a static array is initialized only once (on the first call) and the contrast that a non-static array is re-initialized on every call. Vague statements such as "static is permanent" or "static is fixed" without the initialization point earn nothing. Any wrong statement within a point, such as saying static arrays are re-initialized each call, voids that point.
